title_en: Liu Hongbin v. Beijing Jinglianfa CNC Technology Co., Ltd. and Tianwei Sichuan Silicon Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: The patentee of a utility model patent does not have the right to request another person to cease the implementation of the patent for acts carried out before the announcement date of the grant of the utility model patent. The implementation of the patent by another person before the announcement date of the grant of the utility model patent, including manufacturing, using, selling, offering for sale, and importing the utility model patent product, is not prohibited by the Patent Law, and the related utility model patent product does not constitute an infringing product. Under such circumstances, subsequent acts with respect to the product that has been sold before the announcement date of the grant of the utility model patent, including using, offering for sale, and selling, should be permitted.

full_text_en:
Liu Hongbin v. Beijing Jinglianfa CNC Technology Co., Ltd. and Tianwei Sichuan Silicon Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

[Ruling Summary]

The holder of a utility model patent does not enjoy the right to request others to cease the implementation of the patented utility model before the date of the patent grant announcement. The implementation of the patented utility model by others before the date of the patent grant announcement, including manufacturing, using, offering for sale, selling, and importing the patented utility model product, is not prohibited by the Patent Law, and the relevant utility model patent product does not constitute an infringing product. Under such circumstances, subsequent acts with respect to products already sold before the date of the patent grant announcement, including using, offering for sale, and selling, should be permitted.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Shen Zi No. 1070

Petitioner for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Liu Hongbin, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 25, 1953, residing in Leshan City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xin, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 18, 1966, residing in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, patent agent of Chengdu Tianjia Patent Agency.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Jinglianfa CNC Technology Co., Ltd. Address: No. 80, Kexue Road, Miyun County Economic Development Zone, Beijing City.

Legal Representative: Qin Jianguo, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Pan Guangzhao, lawyer of Beijing Yadong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Tianwei Sichuan Silicon Industry Co., Ltd. Address: Zone B, Xinjin County Industrial Park, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Shujuan, Chairwoman of the Company.

The Petitioner for Retrial, Liu Hongbin, filed a petition with this Court for retrial against the Civil Judgment (2014) Chuan Zhi Min Zhong Zi No. 29 rendered by the Sichuan High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of utility model patent with the Respondents Beijing Jinglianfa CNC Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinglianfa Company) and Tianwei Sichuan Silicon Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianwei Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the case, which has now been concluded.

Liu Hongbin applied for retrial on the following grounds: The second instance judgment erred in finding facts, erred in applying the law, and exceeded the scope of the parties' appeal requests. This case falls under Items (2), (6), and (11) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law). He requested the revocation of the second instance judgment, the affirmation of the first instance judgment, and that the litigation costs of the first and second instances be borne by Jinglianfa Company and Tianwei Company. His main reasons are: (1) The second instance judgment exceeded the scope of the parties' appeal requests. The scope of trial in an appeal case is limited by the scope of the appeal requests, and the court of second instance can only review the facts and application of law related to the appeal requests. In this case, the court of first instance ordered Tianwei Company to immediately cease using the product that infringed the utility model patent right titled "CNC Grinding Machine for Silicon Rod Taper or Outer Circle" with patent number ZL200820223950.0 (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit). Tianwei Company did not appeal this ruling. Under such circumstances, the court of second instance directly modified the judgment, violating legal procedures, and this should be corrected. (2) The second instance judgment erred in finding facts. The sales activity of Jinglianfa Company was not completed before the date of the patent grant announcement. Jinglianfa Company and Tianwei Company signed a "Purchase and Sale Contract" on April 10, 2009, which stipulated conditions for completion of payment, warranty period of the equipment, and responsibilities for replacement and repair of the equipment during the warranty period. According to the contract, the quality guarantee period was one year after delivery and acceptance, and Tianwei Company was to pay Jinglianfa Company 10% of the total contract price as a quality guarantee deposit within one month after the expiration of the guarantee period. Therefore, the actual completion date of the contract performance should be April 9, 2010. A sales activity can have a continuous process, and the time of completion of the sales activity should be determined by the transfer of ownership of the subject matter or the payment of the price. This case should determine the completion time of the sales activity in accordance with Article 11 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) and transaction practices. Therefore, the date of completion of the sales activity in this case should be the date of completion of the performance of the "Purchase and Sale Contract," i.e., April 9, 2010. The second instance court's determination that a sales activity is merely a part of a buying and selling transaction and is a unilateral act of the seller, and that the time of sale cannot be determined by whether the ownership of the subject matter has been transferred or the price has been paid, is erroneous. (3) The second instance judgment erred in applying the law. The second instance court held that since Jinglianfa Company's act of selling the accused infringing product to Tianwei Company did not constitute infringement, Tianwei Company's act of purchasing and using the accused infringing product through lawful channels also did not constitute infringement. The logic and premise of this determination are wrong and lack legal basis. The act of using a product and the acts of manufacturing and selling a product are separate acts that can be distinguished and do not have an inevitable logical relationship. The lawful source of a product does not mean that the act of using it does not constitute infringement. Even if Jinglianfa Company's sales act did not constitute infringement, Tianwei Company's continued use of the infringing product after the date of the patent grant announcement constituted an infringing act. Moreover, Jinglianfa Company continued to infringe after the date of the patent grant announcement.

Jinglianfa Company responded: The second instance judgment clearly found facts, correctly applied the law, and the trial procedure was lawful. Liu Hongbin's grounds for applying for retrial are untenable and should be rejected. Its main reasons are: (1) The acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company occurred before the date of the patent grant announcement. The completion of a sales act should be based on the conclusion or effectiveness of the contract, not on the transfer of ownership of the subject matter or the payment of the price. (2) The utility model patent right takes effect from the date of the patent grant announcement, not from the date of filing. From the date of filing to the date of the patent grant announcement, others' acts of manufacturing or selling products that are the same as the patent application do not constitute infringement. (3) Since Jinglianfa Company's act of selling the accused infringing product to Tianwei Company did not constitute infringement, Tianwei Company's act of purchasing and using the accused infringing product from Jinglianfa Company through lawful channels certainly also did not constitute infringement. Although Tianwei Company did not appeal the first instance judgment, the second instance court's decision to revoke the first instance judgment after Jinglianfa Company's appeal was correct.

During this Court's inquiry, Liu Hongbin further argued that on the day of the second instance court hearing, Jinglianfa Company was still continuing to promote the infringing product on its official website with models and photos of the actual product. The second instance court asked Liu Hongbin to preserve the evidence by notarization, but when the website was accessed at noon that day, the promotional content was no longer available.

This Court holds that, considering the Petitioner for Retrial's grounds for retrial, the Respondents' responses, and the facts of the case, the issues in dispute during the retrial review stage are: Whether the second instance judgment correctly determined that the accused sales act was completed before the date of the patent grant announcement; Whether the second instance judgment correctly determined that Tianwei Company's use act did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit; and Whether the second instance judgment exceeded the scope of the parties' appeal requests.

(I) Whether the second instance judgment correctly determined that the accused sales act was completed before the date of the patent grant announcement

The determination of a sales act in the sense of the Patent Law requires consideration of the legislative purpose of Article 11 of the Patent Law, correct delineation of the relationship between sales acts and offers for sale, and full protection of the interests of the patent holder. Article 11 of the Patent Law provides: "After the grant of the patent right for an invention or utility model, except as otherwise provided for in this Law, no entity or individual may, without the authorization of the patentee, exploit the patent, that is, make, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product, or use the patented process and use, offer to sell, sell, or import the product directly obtained by the patented process, for production or business purposes. After the grant of the patent right for a design, no entity or individual may, without the authorization of the patentee, exploit the patent, that is, make, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented design product, for production or business purposes." The legislative purpose of this article is to clearly define the scope of patent rights, delineate the boundaries between the rights of the patentee and the public, and fully protect the interests of the patentee. This article categorizes acts, providing that holders of invention and utility model patents have five types of rights: making, using, offering for sale, selling, and importing, while holders of design patents have four types: making, offering for sale, selling, and importing. These rights simultaneously constitute the scope of the patentee's right to prohibit and are important standards for determining infringement. To ensure the clarity of the scope of patent rights, enhance predictability, and prevent disputes, the standard for determining the right to sell or sales infringement must be clear, definite, simple, and operable. At the same time, to fully protect the interests of the patentee, the standard for determining sales acts should, as much as possible, achieve a seamless connection between offers for sale and sales acts, so as to cover the relevant transaction links and processes that have a significant impact on the interests of the patentee, thereby more effectively stopping sales infringement. Regarding whether a sales act is completed, Jinglianfa Company argues that the conclusion or effectiveness of the contract should be the standard, while Liu Hongbin argues that the transfer of ownership of the subject matter or the payment of the contract price should be the standard. Therefore, regarding the standard for determining a sales act, there are at least four options: the standard of contract conclusion, the standard of contract effectiveness, the standard of completion of payment, and the standard of delivery or transfer of ownership. If the standard of delivery or transfer of ownership is adopted, the act of the accused infringer from the conclusion of the contract to the delivery or transfer of ownership will not constitute a sale, and this segment will be removed from the scope of the patentee's rights, unduly narrowing the patentee's rights space; moreover, the delivery or transfer of ownership must be judged in conjunction with the specific content of the contract and the performance process, which not only complicates the determination standard but also greatly increases the cost of evidence collection and difficulty of proof for the patentee during enforcement. If the standard of completion of payment is adopted, the act of the accused infringer from the conclusion of the contract to the completion of payment will also not constitute a sale, removing it from the scope of the patentee's rights and narrowing the rights space; moreover, payment involves the contract performance process, and parties may use various methods such as installment payment, set-off, and assignment of claims to perform the contract, which also complicates the determination standard and increases the cost of evidence collection and difficulty of proof for the patentee during enforcement. If the standard of contract effectiveness is adopted, the act from the conclusion of the contract to the effectiveness will also not constitute a sale, removing it from the scope of the patentee's rights and narrowing the rights space; moreover, contract effectiveness is the result of the legal evaluation of the contract's validity, and whether a contract is effective is not entirely dependent on the will of the parties, which is inconsistent with the principle of freedom of will, the basis of tort liability. If the standard of contract conclusion is adopted as the criterion for determining a sales act, since the unilateral expression of intent of a party to sell goods through advertisements, product displays, etc., before the conclusion of the contract constitutes an offer for sale, and the mutual agreement of the parties' expressions of intent to sell goods constitutes a sale, then sales acts and offers for sale can be closely connected, ensuring that there is no gap not covered by the patent right between sales acts and offers for sale, which is conducive to fully protecting the interests of the patentee. At the same time, contract conclusion is a factual state where the parties reach mutual agreement on their expressions of intent to sell goods, often reflected through written contracts and other materials, without the need to further examine the specific terms and performance process of the contract, making it easier for the patentee to obtain evidence and prove the existence of a sales act, with lower costs of evidence collection and determination. Therefore, the determination of a sales act should generally be based on the conclusion of a sales contract. In this case, the "Purchase and Sale Contract" between Tianwei Company and Jinglianfa Company was signed on April 10, 2009, and the sales act in the sense of the Patent Law was implemented on that day, which was earlier than the date of the patent grant announcement (October 21, 2009). The second instance court correctly concluded that the accused sales act of Jinglianfa Company was completed before the date of the patent grant announcement. The corresponding ground for retrial of Liu Hongbin is untenable and is not supported.

(II) Whether the second instance judgment correctly determined that Tianwei Company's use act did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit

The determination of an act infringing a utility model patent right requires a comprehensive consideration of the relevant provisions of the Patent Law and a reasonable balance between the interests of the utility model patent holder and the public. According to Article 11 of the Patent Law, after the grant of a utility model patent, the patent holder acquires the right to prevent others from exploiting the patent without authorization, that is, others may not make, use, offer for sale, sell, or import the patented product of the utility model patent holder for production or business purposes. At the same time, according to Article 40 of the Patent Law, utility model patent rights and design patent rights take effect from the date of the patent grant announcement. It follows that the patent holder does not enjoy the right to request others to cease implementing the patented utility model before the date of the patent grant announcement. The implementation of the patented utility model by others before the date of the patent grant announcement, including manufacturing, using, offering for sale, selling, and importing the patented utility model product, is not prohibited by the Patent Law, and the relevant utility model patent product does not constitute an infringing product. Under such circumstances, subsequent acts with respect to products already sold before the date of the patent grant announcement, including using, offering for sale, and selling, should also be permitted. If a utility model patent holder could, after the date of the patent grant announcement, prohibit subsequent acts with respect to products already sold before that date, it would be equivalent to extending the effect of the utility model patent right after the announcement date to lawful acts before the announcement date, unduly expanding the scope of rights granted to the utility model patent holder by the Patent Law and harming the legitimate interests of the public. In this case, the act of selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company was completed before the date of the patent grant announcement, and such act is not prohibited by the Patent Law. Under such circumstances, Tianwei Company's use of the purchased accused infringing product should also be permitted. Therefore, Tianwei Company's subsequent use act does not infringe the utility model patent right in this case. Liu Hongbin's claim that Tianwei Company's continued use of the infringing product after the date of the patent grant announcement constituted infringing conduct is untenable and is not supported.

(III) Whether the second instance judgment exceeded the scope of the parties' appeal requests

Article 168 of the Civil Procedure Law provides that the people's court of second instance shall review the relevant facts and application of law related to the appeal requests. Accordingly, when hearing an appeal case, the court of second instance should conduct the trial around the parties' appeal requests; matters not raised by the parties shall not be heard, except where the first instance judgment violates prohibitive provisions of the law or harms national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others. In this case, Jinglianfa Company appealed the first instance judgment, requesting the revocation of the first instance judgment and the dismissal of all of Liu Hongbin's claims. The second instance court, focusing on this request, reviewed issues such as whether the act of selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company was completed before the date of the patent grant announcement and whether the acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company constituted infringement. Although Tianwei Company did not appeal the first instance judgment, there is consistency in the litigation interests of Jinglianfa Company and Tianwei Company, and Jinglianfa Company's appeal request necessarily involved the interests of Tianwei Company. After trial, the second instance court found that the acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company occurred before the date of the patent grant announcement, and that the acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product by Jinglianfa Company did not constitute infringement, and Tianwei Company's act of purchasing and using the accused infringing product through lawful channels also did not constitute infringement, and thus Jinglianfa Company's appeal request was upheld. Since there is consistency in the litigation interests of Jinglianfa Company and Tianwei Company, and Jinglianfa Company's appeal request in fact involved the interests of Tianwei Company, the second instance judgment, based on the finding that the acts of both Jinglianfa Company and Tianwei Company did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit, revoked the first instance judgment and dismissed Liu Hongbin's claims. This did not exceed the scope of Jinglianfa Company's appeal request. Liu Hongbin's ground for retrial that the second instance court exceeded the parties' appeal requests is untenable and is not supported.

Furthermore, with respect to Liu Hongbin's assertion that Jinglianfa Company continued to infringe the patent-in-suit during the second instance proceedings, given that Liu Hongbin did not provide sufficient evidence for this assertion and that he may file a separate lawsuit if he obtains relevant evidence, this Court will no longer review this issue.

In conclusion, Liu Hongbin's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Items (2), (6), and (11) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The application for retrial by Liu Hongbin is rejected.
